title: Which Portuguese companies must have an equality plan, and where does training fit?
description: Portugal's Law 62/2017 requires listed and state-owned companies to file annual equality plans by September 15. How CITE's guide builds training into them.
shortAnswer: Under Article 7 of Portugal's Law 62/2017, listed companies and public sector enterprises must prepare an annual equality plan, publish it on their website, and send it to the gender equality commissions CIG and CITE. Normative Order 18/2019 sets a September 15 deadline for the following year's plan. The plan follows a CITE guide whose diagnostic matrix has a dimension on initial and continuous training, including whether the annual training plan contains a module on gender equality and harassment.
keyTakeaways: Article 7(1) of Law 62/2017 requires public sector enterprises and companies listed on a regulated market to prepare annual equality plans and publish them online.

Plans are sent to the Comissão para a Cidadania e a Igualdade de Género (CIG) and the Comissão para a Igualdade no Trabalho e no Emprego (CITE) by September 15 of the year before the plan applies (Normative Order 18/2019, Article 3(4)).
Plans must follow the CITE guide, which covers equal access to employment, working conditions, pay, parental protection, work and life balance, and harassment prevention.

The guide's training dimension asks whether the training plan respects equality, offers equal access to statutory training hours, and includes a module on stereotypes, inclusive language, parental protection, work and life balance, and harassment.
CITE issues recommendations on submitted plans and must publish them by December 20 each year.
regulator: Comissão para a Igualdade no Trabalho e no Emprego (CITE) and Comissão para a Cidadania e a Igualdade de Género (CIG), with the CMVM for listed companies
appliesTo: Companies with shares admitted to trading on a regulated market (empresas cotadas em bolsa)
State public sector enterprises (setor empresarial do Estado)
Local public sector enterprises (setor empresarial local), with adaptations
HR, L&D, and diversity leads who prepare and execute the plan
Boards that approve and publish the plan

blocks.text: [Law 62/2017](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2017/08/14700/0441404416.pdf) of August 1, 2017 (Lei n.º 62/2017, regime da representação equilibrada entre mulheres e homens nos órgãos de administração e de fiscalização das entidades do setor público empresarial e das empresas cotadas em bolsa) does two things. It sets minimum gender thresholds for boards and supervisory bodies, and it requires covered entities to prepare annual equality plans.

The thresholds are 33.3% of each sex for each administrative and supervisory body of public sector enterprises from January 1, 2018 (Article 4), and, for listed companies, 20% of new appointees from the first elective general meeting after January 1, 2018, rising to 33.3% from the first elective general meeting after January 1, 2020 (Article 5). Under Article 6, a listed company that misses the threshold receives a CMVM declaration of non-compliance, then a registered reprimand that is published, and after 360 days a periodic penalty payment.

Article 7 is the part that concerns training. Article 7(1) requires public sector enterprises and listed companies to "elaboram anualmente planos para a igualdade": to prepare annual equality plans aimed at effective equality of treatment and opportunities between women and men, eliminating sex discrimination, and fostering the balance of personal, family, and working life, and to publish them on their website.

sections.heading: How and when must an equality plan be submitted?

blocks.text: Plans are submitted annually through official systems by September 15 of the preceding year. [Normative Order 18/2019](https://cite.gov.pt/documents/14333/137054/DespachoNormativo_18_2019.pdf/7a322dae-156f-4c3f-b0d4-677fa093d1df) of June 21, 2019 (Despacho Normativo n.º 18/2019) sets the procedure.

items: Article 3(1) to (3): state sector enterprises file in the SIOE system, local sector enterprises in the local administration system, and listed companies in the CMVM's information dissemination system (SDI); the plan then reaches CIG and CITE.
Article 3(4): plans for each year must be communicated by September 15 of the previous year. CITE's [equality plans page](https://cite.gov.pt/planos-para-a-igualdade) repeats this deadline.
Article 4(2): the guide covers equal access to employment, equality in working conditions, equal pay, parental protection, and work, family, and personal life balance.
Article 4(4): the published plan must include a section on monitoring its execution.
Article 5: CITE holds at least one annual meeting to approve recommendations on the plans and publishes them by December 20 each year.

blocks.text: Under Article 7(2) of the law, plans must follow the official guide and the materials of the project "Diálogo social e igualdade nas empresas" on CITE's website. Under Article 7(4), CITE may issue recommendations on plans and must publish them online. Law 62/2017 does not set a separate fine for a missing or deficient equality plan; the sanctions in Article 6 relate to the board thresholds.

sections.heading: Where does training appear in the equality plan?

blocks.text: Training appears as a full dimension of the official guide. The [CITE guide for preparing annual equality plans](https://cite.gov.pt/documents/14333/137054/Planos_Igualdade_Guiao.pdf/b4797134-20e2-4132-bbf7-525d5e80a5d6) (Guião para a elaboração dos planos para a igualdade anuais, 2019) contains a diagnostic matrix and a monitoring matrix. Both include a dimension called initial and continuous training (Formação inicial e contínua), alongside dimensions on strategy, access to employment, working conditions, parental protection, work and life balance, and prevention of harassment.
The diagnostic questions in the training dimension include the following, each answered yes or no, with references to the Labor Code.

items: Does the company take account of the principle of equality and non-discrimination between women and men when drawing up its training plan?

Does the annual training plan include a module on equality between women and men, notably on gender stereotypes, inclusive language, parental protection, work, family, and personal life balance, and moral and sexual harassment at work?
Is training offered within normal working hours?
Does the company encourage participation of the under-represented sex in training for professions where one sex is under-represented?
Are trainee profiles in training announcements written for both sexes, without restriction or preference based on sex?
Does the company ensure that women and men have equal access to the number of hours of certified training set by law?

blocks.text: Other dimensions also touch training. The working conditions dimension asks whether the company gives training or guidance to those involved in performance appraisal to prevent gender bias. The monitoring matrix includes, as an example measure, integrating a module on equality between women and men into the annual training plan, with an indicator and a target date.

sections.heading: How should training measures be written into the plan and evidenced?

blocks.text: Each training measure in the plan should have an owner, a budget, an indicator, and evidence, because CITE reviews execution as well as intent. The table below is an illustrative way to turn the guide's training questions into plan measures.

blocks.text: Disaggregating training data by sex is the step most organizations miss. Building it into the [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) from the start makes the annual plan and its monitoring section much easier; see [how to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board).

sections.heading: How do equality plans connect to other Portuguese training duties?

blocks.text: The equality plan does not create new training hours. It looks at how existing training is distributed and what it covers. Two related duties shape the content. The Labor Code gives each worker a minimum number of hours of continuous training a year, which the guide asks companies to distribute equally; see [Portugal's Labor Code continuous training](/regulations/portugal-labour-code-continuous-training). Employers with seven or more workers must also adopt a harassment code of conduct; see [Portugal's workplace harassment prevention obligations](/regulations/portugal-workplace-harassment-prevention-obligations).

Listed companies and state-owned enterprises sit mainly in [financial services](/industries/financial-services) and [energy and resources](/industries/energy-resources), where the plan is often prepared by the same team that runs regulatory training.

As at November 2026, the European Commission's national transposition database lists Law 62/2017 among the measures Portugal notified for Directive (EU) 2022/2381 on gender balance among directors of listed companies, whose transposition deadline was December 28, 2024. CITE's equality plans page still cites Law 62/2017 and Normative Order 18/2019 and lists recommendations up to 2025. This page reflects the published texts of both instruments; check CITE for any updated guide before the next September 15 filing.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats each equality plan training measure as a defined outcome with an owner, an indicator, and evidence, and keeps completion data disaggregated by sex so the monitoring section can be produced from the same records used for the annual training report.

faqs.q: Do private companies that are not listed need an equality plan in Portugal?
faqs.a: Not under Law 62/2017. Article 7 applies to public sector enterprises and companies with shares admitted to trading on a regulated market. Other employers may adopt a plan voluntarily, and CITE's guide and portal can be used for that, but the annual filing duty does not apply to them.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for submitting a Portuguese equality plan?
faqs.a: September 15 of the year before the plan applies. Article 3(4) of Normative Order 18/2019 states that plans for each year must be communicated by September 15 of the previous year, and CITE's equality plans page repeats that date.

faqs.q: Does the equality plan have to include harassment training?
faqs.a: The guide asks whether the annual training plan includes a module on equality topics, including moral and sexual harassment at work, and it has a separate dimension on preventing harassment. In the diagnostic matrix, each no answer points the company to a CITE support alert explaining the relevant legal provisions and practice.

faqs.q: What happens after the plan is filed?
faqs.a: CITE analyzes the plans and approves recommendations at least once a year, publishing them by December 20 under Article 5 of Normative Order 18/2019. Companies are expected to act on recommendations and report execution in the monitoring section of the next published plan.
